title: The Old Woman and the Wine-Jar
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: An old Woman picked up an empty Wine-jar which had once contained a rare and costly wine, and which still retained some traces of its exquisite bouquet. She raised it to her nose and sniffed at it again and again. "Ah," she cried, "how delicious must have been the liquid which has left behind so ravishing a smell."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the old Woman pick up?
options: A jar full of fresh wine
A basket of grapes
An empty Wine-jar
A broken clay pot

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what had the Wine-jar once contained?
options: A rare and costly wine
A common, everyday wine
Water used for cooking
Oil used for cooking and lamps

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Wine-jar still retain?
options: A small amount of the actual wine
A label naming its origin
A crack from being dropped
Some traces of its exquisite bouquet

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Woman do with the jar?
options: She fills it with fresh water to drink
She raises it to her nose and sniffs at it again and again
She sells it at the local market
She breaks it open to check inside

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Woman exclaim about the wine that once filled the jar?
options: That it must have been very cheap to produce
That it must have spoiled a long time ago
That it must have been delicious, given the smell it left behind
That she wishes she could find more like it nearby

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how does the Woman judge the quality of the original wine?
options: By reasoning from the lingering scent left in the empty jar
By tasting a few remaining drops inside
By reading a label attached to the jar
By asking someone who had tasted it before

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Woman's repeated sniffing suggest about her reaction to the smell?
options: She is trying to determine if the jar is actually empty
She is checking whether the jar is safe to drink from
She is confused about what kind of jar it is
She finds the lingering scent so pleasant that she wants to experience it fully

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "bouquet" mean in "its exquisite bouquet"?
options: A bundle of fresh flowers
A pleasant, distinctive smell, especially of wine
A formal announcement or toast
A collection of old pottery

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "ravishing" mean in "so ravishing a smell"?
options: Faint and barely noticeable
Sour and unpleasant
Extremely delightful or captivating
Ordinary and unremarkable

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: The lingering trace of something excellent can hint at how wonderful the thing itself must have been
Empty containers are always more valuable than full ones
Old women are especially skilled at judging the quality of wine
Smell is a more reliable sense than taste for judging wine

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what condition is the Wine-jar in when the Woman finds it?
options: Still half full
Cracked and leaking
Sealed shut
Empty

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how many times does the Woman sniff the jar?
options: Only once
Again and again
Exactly twice
She does not sniff it at all

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what single word does the Woman use to begin her exclamation?
options: "Oh"
"My"
"Ah"
"Well"

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Woman describe the wine as delicious even though she never tasted it?
options: She infers its quality from the powerful impression its scent still makes
She had tasted the exact same wine once before, long ago
She read a description of the wine written on the jar
She is simply guessing without any real basis for her claim

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the phrase "rare and costly wine" suggest about the drink that once filled the jar?
options: It was cheap and easy to find in most markets
It was made specifically for the old Woman
It was no longer produced anywhere in the region
It was unusual and expensive, not an everyday sort of wine

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "retained" mean in "still retained some traces"?
options: Completely lost
Kept or held onto
Replaced with something new
Hidden from view

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: An old Woman finds a jar still full of rare wine
An old Woman is disappointed to find the jar completely empty and scentless
An old Woman marvels at the delicious wine she imagines once filled a jar, based only on its lingering scent
An old Woman sells the empty jar at the market
